newsitem.title: USA: ACLU, Planned Parenthood challenge R.I. abortion ban.
newsitem.headline: ACLU, Planned Parenthood challenge R.I. abortion ban.

text.p: The American Civil Liberties Union filed suit against Rhode Island Wednesday challenging the constitutionality of the state's so-called "partial birth abortion" ban.

Gov. Lincoln Almond signed the Rhode Island law last week. The measure barring the intact dilation and extraction procedure mirrors one vetoed by President Clinton last year. Clinton has said he will veto a similar bill passed by Congress again this year.

The lawsuit, brought on behalf of Planned Parenthood of Rhode Island and two doctors, contends the measure is so vague that physicians potentially face criminal and civil penalties for performing almost any abortion by any method after the first trimester of pregnancy.

"Proponents of the ban purport to be targeting a single procedure...so called 'partial birth abortions.' But that term has no medical meaning and the law's definition is so poorly drafted it could encompass the safest and most common abortion methods used," said Catherine Weiss, director of the ACLU's reproductive freedom project.
ACLU spokesman Steven Brown said his organization would be seeking a temporary restraining order to stop enforcement of the law and he expected a hearing on the matter shortly.
The procedure involves the partial extraction of the fetus feet first, the subsequent suctioning out of the brain and the removal of the fetus.
